title: Bounding Box Calculator: Centre Plus Radius
description: Build a latitude/longitude bounding box from a centre and radius with the Bounding Box Calculator — for API queries and spatial filters. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 10-kilometre box around Times Square runs from 40.6679 to 40.8481 latitude and −74.1039 to −73.8671 longitude — computed, ready to paste into an API call.
quick_answer: The Bounding Box Calculator takes a centre coordinate and radius and returns the latitude/longitude bounding box around it — the min/max extent APIs, map queries and spatial filters ask for. Enter centre and radius and copy the four numbers that turn a circle into a rectangle a database can search.

body.t: Overpass, geocoding and places APIs filter by bbox. Compute the extent here instead of guessing degree offsets — the
The classic two-step: cheap bbox filter first, exact distance second. The box this page builds is step one done correctly at any latitude.
Tile and feature requests need extents in degrees — the centre-plus-radius form is how humans think, the box is how servers answer.
Clip a dataset to 'around here' before the heavy geometry starts. The box is the coarse knife that saves the fine one.

Centre 40.7580, −73.9855, radius 10 km → box lat 40.6679…40.8481, lon −74.1039…−73.8671. Note the longitude span (0.2368°) is wider than the latitude span (0.1802°) — at 41°N, degrees of longitude are shorter, so more of them fit in 10 km.

faq: Is the box the same as a radius circle?
No — the box is the circle's square envelope: it contains the circle plus four corner regions outside it. Use the box to fetch candidates, then true distance to judge them.
Is longitude handling exact near the poles?
The calculator widens the longitude span as latitude rises and treats polar cases by its stated method — a radius reaching the pole spans all longitudes, and honest tools say so.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — the extent your APIs expect.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
The box inherits the centre's accuracy; extra decimals in the output are arithmetic, not knowledge.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Yes — the four values paste into extent fields everywhere; mind each product's axis order.
Why is the longitude span wider than latitude's?
Longitude degrees shrink toward the poles (84.4 km at New York's latitude against 111.0 for latitude). The box compensates — eyeballing equal degree offsets is the amateur error this page prevents.
Kilometres or miles?
Both units are accepted for the radius, per this site's convention.
Date-line centres?
A centre near ±180° produces a box that wraps; split it into two queries for APIs that cannot wrap.
How big a radius is sane?
Boxes are for local extents. Continental radii belong to polygon filters, not envelopes — the corners' distortion grows with size.
Antimeridian and poles aside — marine use?
Fisheries and shipping queries use bboxes heavily; the same envelope logic applies, with the corner warning doubled at sea.
Can I build the box from two corners instead?
That is the Coordinate Bounding Box Generator's shape — corners in, normalised extent out.
